name: Metaplanet

snapshot.holdings: 44,000 BTC (as of most recent disclosed accumulation, per October 2026 purchase disclosures)

email_summary: Morgan Stanley group's Metaplanet stake fell from 5.25% to 2.51% in a Nov 6 filing tied to securities-lending activity, not a clear directional signal.
bottom_line: The only confirmed development inside the 3-day window is a large-shareholder report showing Morgan Stanley-affiliated entities cutting their combined Metaplanet stake below the 5% disclosure threshold, but the stated holding purpose was securities-business/lending, not an investment view, so read-through to thesis is limited. The bigger near-term catalyst remains MSCI's final index-exclusion list due November 11, which was already flagged and has not yet been resolved.
source_conflicts: BTC holdings figures conflict across sources: some trackers still show 40,177 BTC (as of Q1 2026 purchase) while others show 44,000 BTC (as of October 2026 purchases); no new BTC purchase was disclosed in the Nov 6-9 window.

Share count and market cap figures conflict across data providers: one source lists 307,570,337 total issued shares while market-cap figures from other aggregators imply a much larger share base, likely reflecting treasury-share or reporting-date differences.
mNAV estimates conflict across providers (one third-party site shows ~1.21x using a 40,177 BTC base), so no single current mNAV figure can be confirmed as of this sweep.

updates.headline: Morgan Stanley group cuts Metaplanet stake to 2.51%
updates.what_happened: Morgan Stanley MUFG Securities and affiliated entities filed a change report with Japan's Kanto Local Finance Bureau on November 6 showing their combined Metaplanet stake fell from 5.25% to 2.51%, with the reporting obligation date set at October 30. The filing breaks out the reduction across Morgan Stanley MUFG Securities, Morgan Stanley & Co. International plc, and Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, with the UK entity's stake falling from 3.64% to 1.48%.
updates.thesis_fit: This is a large-shareholder reduction below the 5% disclosure threshold per the monitoring checklist, but the group's prior filing stated the holding was for 'securities business' and 'securities lending' purposes rather than long-term investment conviction, so it likely reflects prime-brokerage/stock-lending flow rather than a bearish institutional view on the stock.
